summary.headline: Scoda Tubes Q2 FY27 revenue rose just 2.5% to INR148.9 crore while operating EBITDA margin fell 479 bps to 10.6%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was broadly flat year-on-year at INR148.9 crore, with H1 FY27 revenue up 12.6% to INR273.3 crore. Operating EBITDA fell to INR15.8 crore from INR22.3 crore, as power, fuel and freight costs rose and private-player competition stopped price hikes. Inventory built up as production stayed high and sales conversion slowed. Management reiterated 20-25% FY27 revenue growth guidance, pinned on the welded expansion starting trial production in Q4 FY27, but declined to give margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +2.5% YoY vs INR145.3 crore in Q2 FY26
+12.6% YoY vs INR242.7 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Domestic INR93.8 crore (63%); export INR55.1 crore (37%)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR22.3 crore in Q2 FY26
mainly machinery shipments and solar plant
long-term debt up from about INR40 crore to nearly INR100 crore per analyst

segments.name: Seamless pipes
segments.commentary: Order book about INR185 crore, of which roughly 40% is export (US and Europe customers); execution time about 4-5 months. Management targets about 70% capacity utilisation in FY27, rising to 80-85% next year; 80-85% is the stated optimum. Seamless working capital cycle about 180-185 days.

segments.name: Welded pipes
segments.commentary: Expansion extends capability to 16-inch pipe; trial production in Q4 FY27 and revenue from January 2027. Welded working capital cycle about 130-140 days; gross margin about 25%, versus about 32-33% in seamless. Target end-markets: data centres, HVAC, cooling, industrial water treatment and desalination.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% reiterated; analyst computed this implies about 30-35% YoY growth in H2, which management did not dispute.
Management said Europe, despite the quota regime, is on track for its 25% annual growth guidance.
No specific EBITDA margin guidance; management said it is premature given geopolitical uncertainty, and that its priority is protecting the Q2 FY27 margin level.
Peak debt expected at INR250 crore, with no immediate plans to reduce it.
Additional 8,000 MTPA welded brownfield capacity (about INR40-45 crore capex) expected in April-June 2027 (H1 FY28), taking total welded capacity to 21,150 MTPA.
Internal capex targets are 15-20% IRR; long-term ROCE target 15-20%.
capex_capacity: Welded expansion to 16-inch pipe: trial production in Q4 FY27 (Jan 2027 revenue start, per management); solar for welded operations also due Q4 FY27.

Additional 8,000 MTPA brownfield welded capacity: civil works under way, long-lead equipment procurement on track, commissioning H1 FY28; capex about INR40-45 crore, funded by internal accruals and long-term debt.
Captive solar: 4.99 MW DC for seamless operations energised and grid-synchronised in August 2026, already offsetting power cost.

Management said remaining capex on the 20,000 MTPA programme is budgeted at about INR45 crore for the 8,000 MTPA addition, with a further INR40-50 crore for the remaining 12,000 MTPA. Analyst's 20,000 MTPA reading was clarified as 8,000 MTPA. No other capex is planned.
Seamless capacity utilisation: about 70% targeted for FY27; company declined to disclose the FY27 actual.
RINA Marine audit completed July 2026; final approval awaited.
demand_pricing: Seamless competition: about 60,000-70,000 MTPA of new private seamless capacity (hot and cold) cited; management said it limits price pass-through, so realisations are largely flat.

Domestic revenue fell about 12% in Q2; oil and gas demand weak, with capex deferred and higher crude prices. Power sector (BHEL, NTPC) and some chemicals are the main domestic demand sources; BHEL tender timing is uncertain.
Export: Europe slowed under EU quota and anti-dumping duty regime (duty rates 5-25% per quarter); customers moving to quarterly buying and bonded warehouses. US performing well.
Management said revenue growth in Q2 came from volume rather than value, because of pricing pressure.
Chinese imports of ordinary grades said to be falling to near negligible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the welded line delayed, and when does the 8,000 MT line start?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction slipped 2-3 months after gas-supply disruptions in March-April 2026. Welded revenue from January 2027; the 8,000 MT line is expected around April-June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 15-16%, or do they settle at 11-13% given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Power and fuel rose from 3% to 4.9% of revenue and freight from 1.4% to 2.9%. Competition blocked price hikes. Management declined to give margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did long-term debt rise, and what is peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt funded the 8,000 MT welded capacity and about 9 MW ground-mounted solar. Peak debt is INR250 crore with no near-term reduction plans.

qa_highlights.question: What are the welded-segment working capital cycle and the inventory outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Welded cycle is 130-140 days versus 180-185 days for seamless. Inventory days rose on higher production and slower sales conversion; management expects normalisation in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the seamless capacity utilisation and optimum level?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% in FY27 (not disclosed as actual); optimum is 80-85%, targeted for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR185 crore, roughly 40% exports; executed in 4-5 months; oil and gas softer, other sectors stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Is the moat intact against private competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited specialised SS production, approvals, accreditations and customer and export diversification. It said the current downturn is a rough patch and expects improvement after January-February 2027.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin at 10.6% in Q2 with no guidance; power, fuel and freight costs remain high and pass-through is limited.
Inventory build-up and working capital intensity (cash conversion weak); management expects normalisation in H2 FY27.
Debt rising toward INR250 crore peak; interest burden against flat revenue.
Welded trial production and revenue timing (Q4 FY27 / January 2027) and the 20-25% growth guidance, which implies a sharp H2 step-up.
Seamless capacity additions of 60,000-70,000 MTPA; EU quota regime and anti-dumping duty affecting European exports; BHEL tender timing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term prospects and the welded expansion, but cautious on near term. Management repeatedly declined to give margin, utilisation, per-tonne and cash-flow figures, citing competition and geopolitical uncertainty. Its answers on the Q2 margin and revenue shortfall leaned on general statements.
key_quotes: This is a rough patch which we have not seen since last 10 years.
Given the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and the limited visibility on how the situation may evolve, we believe it would be premature to provide specific margin guidance at this stage.
We remain confident of achieving approximately 70% capacity utilization for seamless product in FY27.

adds.what: Welded expansion to 16-inch pipe (trial production, revenue from January 2027)
Additional 8,000 MTPA brownfield welded capacity (total welded to 21,150 MTPA)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% is reiterated, but Q2 revenue was up only 2.5% with H1 at +12.6%, so H2 would need about 30-35% growth; backing is capacity (welded 16-inch trial in Q4 FY27, revenue from January 2027) plus an 8,000 MTPA welded addition in H1 FY28, with no quantified order or volume bridge for the H2 step-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA margin fell 479 bps to 10.6% (from 15.38%) as power and fuel rose from 3% to 4.9% of revenue and freight from 1.4% to 2.9%, and private competition blocks price hikes; management gave no margin guidance and is only protecting the Q2 level.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Welded 16-inch expansion has trial production in Q4 FY27 with revenue from January 2027, and the 8,000 MTPA brownfield welded addition (total 21,150 MTPA) is due April-June 2027 with civil works under way and capex about INR40-45 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue grew 12.6% but Q2 only 2.5%, and FY27 guidance of 20-25% implies about 30-35% H2 growth; volume growth is backed by welded capacity from January 2027 and 8,000 MTPA in H1 FY28, but seamless utilisation is only targeted at about 70% and no order bridge was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already committed (about INR45 crore for the 8,000 MTPA addition plus INR40-50 crore for the remaining 12,000 MTPA) and management said no other capex is planned; seamless utilisation is about 70%, below the 80%+ level that would force a new announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose only 2.5% and the FY27 20-25% guidance was reiterated but not raised, while analysts see the H2 step-up as demanding and management gave no margin guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue growth of 12.6% needs about 30-35% H2 growth to hit the 20-25% FY27 target, with welded revenue only from January 2027, Europe slowed by EU quotas and duties, and domestic revenue down about 12% in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The welded expansion to 16-inch pipe is in trial production in Q4 FY27 with revenue from January 2027, targeting data centres, HVAC, cooling and desalination.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation in H2 FY27
rows.why: Inventory built up in Q2 on higher production and slower sales conversion; management expects normalisation in H2, but seamless working capital cycle is 180-185 days and welded 130-140 days.

rows.label: Peak debt at INR250 crore, no near-term reduction
rows.why: Gross borrowings were INR229.2 crore at 30 Sep 2026, with peak debt guided at INR250 crore and no immediate plans to reduce it, funding the welded and solar capex.

rows.label: Europe on track for 25% growth despite EU quotas
rows.why: Management says Europe is on track for 25% annual growth, but EU quota and anti-dumping duties (5-25%) are slowing buying and export revenue was INR55.1 crore (37%) in Q2.

tone.note: Management was confident on the welded expansion, the 16-inch launch and long-term prospects, but cautious on near-term margins and declined to give margin, utilisation and cash-flow figures; analysts pressed on the H2 step-up needed for 20-25% growth and margin recovery.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue grew only 2.5% to INR148.9 crore, and management attributed that growth to volume rather than price, with seamless realisations flat under private-capacity pressure and domestic revenue down about 12%; no one-off items are stated, but the weak quarterly growth is a base-quality concern rather than a one-off.
